=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:172-178,1050-1071 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The collect stage accepts a supersede candidate through the general trusted-author rule in triage_supersede_candidate (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, or github-actions[bot]) and clears EXISTING at line 1065. It never checks that the old issue was opened by the authenticated account; that check runs only in triage_supersede_stale_issue, after the new issue has been filed (.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml lines 737-746 / 745-746).
  WHY: When the old ai:blocked issue was opened by another account, or the identity read fails, a new issue is filed and supersede then skips with not_own_issue or identity_unavailable. That leaves two open issues with the same fingerprint, so later runs hit multiple_open and then duplicate_open_issue, and the stale issue can never be superseded. All reviewers rated it MAJOR (mapped to high). sonnet-5_5 and minimax-m3 also call the github-actions[bot] trust branch effectively dead for supersede.
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:239-246 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The re-read jq filter in triage_supersede_stale_issue outputs `foreign_author` when `.user.login` is missing (for example on a 404 error body). Under pipefail plus `|| echo unreadable`, that can give a two-line value that is quietly reclassified as `old_issue_unreadable`.
  WHY: The skip-reason classification depends on an accidental mix of jq output and the fallback echo, so a read failure can be reported under the wrong reason. It is still safe because no write happens. Source rated NIT (mapped to low). anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and minimax_minimax-m3 gave the same 1-line fix as a non-blocking HARDENING_SUGGESTION.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Issue #8671, Approach C: "if EXISTING carries ai:blocked, was opened by the authenticated account, its body's Head SHA is a 40-hex SHA different from the new failure's HEAD_SHA, and HEAD_SHA equals PR_HEAD_SHA_CURRENT, then: post one comment ... close it as not_planned, and continue to file the new issue; ... otherwise keep today's skip reason=duplicate_open_issue."
  expected_change_site: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh, the dedup supersede decision (the triage_supersede_candidate call and the `EXISTING=""` assignment at line 1065, around lines 1056-1065), or the post step in .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml before `gh issue create`
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The authenticated-account condition exists only in triage_supersede_stale_issue (lines 232-244 / 241-248 / 232-243), which runs after the new issue is created (workflow lines 737-746). triage_supersede_candidate (lines 172-178 / 174-178) checks only the general association rule (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR or github-actions[bot]). No code on the file-or-skip path compares the old issue's author with the authenticated login. When the author does not match, or the identity read fails, a new issue is filed and the old one stays open, instead of keeping duplicate_open_issue.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:triage_supersede_candidate lines 174-178; dedup branch at line 1065 (`EXISTING=""`); triage_supersede_stale_issue lines 232-244; .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml lines 737-746 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The "opened by the authenticated account" check was added only to the post-create supersede stage. Collect still accepts any OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR or github-actions[bot] author and clears EXISTING. Collect runs with GH_PAT and post/supersede runs with CHECK_TRIAGE_ISSUES_TOKEN, so collect cannot know the posting login. When the author is foreign, or the identity is unavailable, the post step creates the new issue, then logs `op=supersede outcome=skip reason=not_own_issue` and leaves the old one open.
  WHY: Two open issues share the fingerprint, so the next failure gets `skip multiple_open` and then `skip reason=duplicate_open_issue`, and the stale issue is never superseded. The github-actions[bot] branch at line 176 is effectively dead. Fix: move the identity read and the old-issue author re-read into the post step, before `gh issue create`, using the issues token. Alternative: drop the Bot branch and refuse the candidate in collect.
- TASK_GAP | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  Requirement: Issue #8671, Approach C: "if EXISTING carries ai:blocked, was opened by the authenticated account, its body's Head SHA is a 40-hex SHA different from the new failure's HEAD_SHA, and HEAD_SHA equals PR_HEAD_SHA_CURRENT, then: post one comment ... close it as not_planned, and continue to file the new issue; ... otherwise keep today's skip reason=duplicate_open_issue."
  Expected change site: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh, the dedup supersede decision (the triage_supersede_candidate call and `EXISTING=""` at line 1065), or the post step in .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml before `gh issue create`.
  Evidence of absence: The authenticated-account condition exists only in triage_supersede_stale_issue (lines 232-244), which runs after creation (workflow lines 737-746). No author-vs-login comparison happens on the file-or-skip path. Same root cause as the correctness finding.
- HARDENING: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh, triage_supersede_stale_issue, re-read jq filter at line 240 | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=1
  PROBLEM: An error body (for example a 404) has no `.user.login`, so the filter emits "foreign_author". Only `set -o pipefail` (line 92) plus the `|| echo unreadable` fallback turn that into "unreadable". The outcome is safe, but it relies on accidental two-line output.
  WHY: Suggested fix: `if (.state | type) != "string" then "unreadable" elif (.user.login // "") != $login then "foreign_author" elif ... end` (1 line).
- NOTE: The copilot-pull-request-reviewer check failed with HTTP 422 custom_instructions_too_large. This is caused by the external action's prompt size (AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md being loaded), not by the diff. The pass-1 finding that attributes it to triage_supersede_stale_issue is not supported.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1050-1070 (in the collect stage) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Collect-stage dedup clears EXISTING (EXISTING="") because the issue is a candidate in triage_supersede_candidate. It does not verify the "opened by authenticated account" check from triage_supersede_stale_issue.
  WHY: If another authorized user opened the old issue, the post-create supersede fails with not_own_issue or identity_unavailable and both issues stay open. Later runs then always skip with duplicate_open_issue, and the stale issue can never be superseded automatically.
- HARDENING: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh, triage_supersede_stale_issue, jq filter | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=1
  PROBLEM: The loose check (`if (.state == "open") and ... else "stale" end`) means an unreadable gh api response accidentally triggers the "stale" classification.
  WHY: Suggested fix: if (.state | type) != "string" then "unreadable" elif (.state == "open") and ... then "eligible" else "stale" end (1 line).
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:triage_supersede_candidate trust check at lines 172-178; collect-stage dedup branch assigning EXISTING="" (around lines 1056-1065) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The collect-stage trust rule (User with OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, or Bot github-actions[bot]) clears EXISTING and files a new triage issue. The authenticated-account check (gh api user + jq compare) runs only in triage_supersede_stale_issue, after creation. On a mismatch, or identity_unavailable, it logs not_own_issue / identity_unavailable and returns 0 without writing anything.
  WHY: Two open issues share the fingerprint, so the next failure gets skip reason=multiple_open and then skip reason=duplicate_open_issue. The stale issue can never be superseded, which is the regression the PR is meant to prevent. The github-actions[bot] branch is dead weight whenever CHECK_TRIAGE_ISSUES_TOKEN maps to a different bot identity (e.g. shubhodeep1-bot[bot], claude-bot[bot]).
- TASK_GAP | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  Requirement: "if EXISTING carries ai:blocked, was opened by the authenticated account, its body's Head SHA is a 40-hex SHA different from the new failure's HEAD_SHA, and HEAD_SHA equals PR_HEAD_SHA_CURRENT, then: post one comment ... and continue to file the new issue; ... otherwise keep today's skip reason=duplicate_open_issue" (linked issue #8671, Approach C).
  Expected change site: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh, the dedup supersede decision: the triage_supersede_candidate invocation and the EXISTING="" assignment in the normal-mode dedup branch (around lines 1056-1065).
  Evidence of absence: triage_supersede_candidate (lines 172-178) checks only the association rule. The authenticated-account condition exists only in triage_supersede_stale_issue (lines 241-248), after filing. On a login mismatch the diff files a new issue and leaves the old one open, instead of keeping skip reason=duplicate_open_issue.
- HARDENING: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh, post-create old-issue re-read jq filter in triage_supersede_stale_issue | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=1
  PROBLEM: A non-JSON or error body (403/404, with no .user.login) falls through to foreign_author, and the `|| echo unreadable` pipefail fallback appends a second line.
  WHY: Suggested fix: `if (.state | type) != "string" then "unreadable" elif (.user.login // "") != $login ...` (1 line).
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  Requirement: "If EXISTING carries ai:blocked, was opened by the authenticated account, its body's Head SHA is a 40-hex SHA different from the new failure's HEAD_SHA, and HEAD_SHA equals PR_HEAD_SHA_CURRENT, then" supersede it; "otherwise keep today's skip reason=duplicate_open_issue."
  Expected change site: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh, the dedup supersede decision in triage_supersede_candidate and the branch that clears EXISTING.
  Evidence of absence: The candidate check accepts any trusted OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR or github-actions[bot] author at lines 174-178, and the dedup branch clears EXISTING at line 1065. The authenticated-account comparison happens only in triage_supersede_stale_issue at lines 232-243, after the new issue is created. A different trusted author, or a failed identity read, therefore files a new issue and skips closing the old one.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1052-1071 (candidate acceptance and `EXISTING=""` clear at 1065), trusted-author filter at 174-178; authenticated-account gate only in `triage_supersede_stale_issue` at 229-248 (invoked at .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:745-746) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Collect-stage candidate selection trusts the old issue through the generic allowlist and never compares its author with the authenticated login. That condition is enforced only after the new issue has been filed.
  WHY: When a different trusted account (e.g. a human OWNER) opened the stale blocked issue, collect clears EXISTING and files a new issue, then supersede skips with `reason=not_own_issue`. Two triage issues stay open for the fingerprint, later failures dedup against `first` (line 1047), and the stale issue stays open indefinitely.
